Weekly Digest: First Playable Gets a Date, the Code Foundation Lands

Weekly Digest · Sep 06 – Sep 13, 2026 · 1293 messages from 119 members

Hello, jammers! This was a big organizing week for ASGC Game Jam 2026: 1,293 messages from 119 active members, a First Playable target date, the merge that lays the code foundation, and a lot of cross-pod alignment. Here's what happened between Sep 6 and Sep 13.

🎯 First Playable: October 10th

After Tuesday's director meeting, Cafedunoir held a GitHub backlog prioritization session with Matt Barnes and VibeBlind (Seth). She then announced in #🎯│director-discussion that the team is targeting a First Playable by the end of Sprint 6 (October 10th). The scope:

  • Player Character
  • Traversal (swimming, ballast, terrestrial walking)
  • Oxygen System
  • Foundational system communication and target locking, as groundwork for Investigation

Async feedback is welcome in the thread. Definitions for Alpha, Beta and first Public Release will be aligned at next week's director call.

Before that meeting, VibeBlind pushed the team to think in iterable pieces. A lot of ideas aren't out of scope, they're just not next. shadowarrior made the case that a playable keeps every department aligned. In #❔tech-questions❔, VibeBlind also said he wants to cut per-feature process from about 15 pages down to roughly 2 (Design→Tech and Tech→QA).

Also from directors: Ridley pointed out that the NPC like/trust score in the character template isn't covered by any feature doc. Matt says it isn't planned yet, but it isn't off the table either. Leadership will discuss it.

💻 PR #158 Lands, Now Go Grab a Ticket

Carlos Ortiz's foundational PR #158 introduces Atlantis___ class naming, C++ base classes, reparented Blueprints and detailed docs. After reviews from Awesomeosity and dbugslayer, Xandemon approved and merged it on Sep 10 so every pod has a shared baseline. Carlos's position on C++ vs Blueprints is that either is fine and "done is better than optimized."

Carlos followed up with the most-reacted post of the week (+18) in #🎯│tech-discussions. Don't wait to be assigned work: find or create tickets in the Git backlog, over-communicate with your pod PoCs, and keep main safe.

Other tech news: - VibeBlind posted first-draft TDS specs as GitHub issues for Investigation (TDS-005-001 to 004), Journal (006-001 to 006) and Dialogue (008-001 to 006). KyotoRando answered with "No notes, just kudos!" - In #Player Character, Swart Tigerhorn posted a revised TDD-000 (#115), and he and Carlos debated whether player state belongs in its scope. Carlos is taking on the base classes and the TDD work except the camera. Diana Donado is the new Feature Owner, and shoe joined as Art POC. - In the Journal pod, ogam proposed a pub/sub UAtlantisJournalSubsystem and started the main UI widget on branch 121-journal-data. - In #Water, sevenn4 fixed his Gitea push problems by creating an access token. Xandemon's advice: one PR per "initial implementation" issue, then smaller follow-up branches.

ogam's diagrams of the message pipeline between game systems, the Journal subsystem and the UI — by ogam in #[Feature] FDS-006 Journal

🫧 Cross-Pod Alignment: Oxygen, Investigation, Journal & Dialogue

Oxygen (Sep 10): David "AssassinCS" Thompson organized a cross-pod alignment meeting. underwolf's notes and his updated FDS-003 doc cover the proposals: - No more passive oxygen drain - A new meditation mechanic that regenerates oxygen at safe spots, which Ridley pitched from the Narrative side - Normal combat actions cost 0 oxygen - Stealth allocates a percentage of oxygen on entry

Still open: who owns player health (raised by TreeckoRalts), how the Ammo vs Oxygen split works, and who owns movement state. In #[Feature] FDS-010 Stealth, Awesomeosity argued that Traversal should provide movement state, and Stealth will consume it. Combat won't happen while swimming.

For Traversal, the sprint goal is a Blueprint prototype: ballast first, then swimming, then walking. Ascending and descending are free; holding a depth costs oxygen.

Investigation/Journal/Dialogue (Sep 7): The recording failed, so KyotoRando (Clayton) posted manual notes: - No Investigation-specific progress UI - Dialogue flags become Journal entries written as internal monologue - Journal owns the minimap - Accessibility ideas include a gossip sound "radar" - The game is targeted at about 6 hours

Anrakyr (Arda) got the Investigation lead role and confirmed that several investigations can run at once. binarie pitched a mindmap-style journal.

Screenshot of the Examine Mode section of the Investigation design doc, explaining the first-person view — by Anrakyr in #[Feature] FDS-005 Investigation

🛠️ Tooling Pains & Process Fixes

  • ClickUp permissions broke the async stand-up. Cafedunoir called it a lesson learned: future async stand-ups will run as Discord threads.
  • David found the root cause in #🗓️│production-lead-discussion. Limited Members only see spaces explicitly shared with them, so their access toggle has to be switched ON. About 80 people are fixed and roughly 200 still need it, so helping hands are welcome.
  • VibeBlind will mirror the ClickUp standards into GitHub's Tech Standards.md. klight pitched Carlos's Keystone app to replace the scattered When2Meets.
  • Felix's tool can now edit ClickUp, and he got access to the GitHub backlog to look at pulling in GitHub data.
  • Carlos's Tech Producer roll call aims to move Traversal and Combat from "figuring it out" to actual coding.

📚 Narrative: Dependencies & Blocked Pods

Themes and premise are finalized. The high-level plot outline is due at the end of the sprint. Until it lands, several pods are waiting:

  • Quest Design spent the week without a confirmed Design point of contact. butchbear shared Matt's guidance: "you tell us what and we tell you how." The Quest Design Mock-Up is now final.
  • District Design, Resource Economy, NPC Interactions and Characters & Cinematics are blocked on Narrative decisions. Vincent stepped in as District Design's Production PoC.
  • butchbear passed along that the world may shrink to one level plus a tutorial cave.
  • Lianhua, MAR and Laura opened the Steampunk Bible to all writers, with contributions due by the 14th. Ridley wants writers to focus first on how the tech actually works.
  • Dreaa stepped down as a design lead because of crunch at their day job, but hopes to stay on as an IC.

This week's Narrative standup notes compiled from the producer updates — by YosephAlex4nder in #Production Handoffs

🎨 Art, Tech Art, Audio & Builds

  • sevenn4 pushed the underwater visuals branch, three M_SeaSandyGround variants and a Substance Designer template. Anki reviewed the post-process distortion and claimed shimmer, footprints and dust. Zef's advice on ground height: start cheap, upgrade later.
  • Brandon Trabon sculpted the player character's suit and face, working from feedback by LazyMonkey and a paintover by Zef.
  • VarunP shared a whale shop interior concept, and Mollunn sculpted their first wood trim.
  • Zef set out an interim process for art requests: check with the art PoC, then the producer creates a ClickUp task for TJ, Devang or Zef.
  • LockedInFish's tutorial cave music went to V2 the same day after NateTheMood's feedback. Nate also posted the OST bounty board requirements.
  • QA signed off on a build, and AaronBurrSir promoted QA_TESTING to Default. His Steam key thread drew about 60 requests, with keys going out via DM.
  • In #🎯│leads-discussion, the leads are leaning toward a "revised NDA" that lets people share work with a WIP disclaimer. Nothing is final yet.
  • For fun, Lianhua started get-to-know-you threads on favorite books, games, shows and music.

Quotes of the week

So for the defining functional or playable, I think the question should be less what features are in the demo/alpha and more what is the smallest coherent version of the game we can play next, and what work is preventing us from getting there?

— VibeBlind in #Hey all - looking forward to our next (jump)

Combo is preferred; imo, done is better than optimized and I personally don't care if participants implement things in C++ or BLueprints unless it breaks stuff or slows the game to an unplayable crawl.

— Carlos Ortiz in #Draft for TDS-000 base classes (jump)

@Cafedunoir I've found the root cause of the ClickUp problems: the assignment failures and the access complaints from people who were already added are the same issue.

Guests and limited members only get access to locations and items explicitly shared with them. If a participant hasn't been shared into the right locations, they can't see their work even if the space is globally visible and we can't assign them tasks, even though they show up as added.

Source: https://help.clickup.com/hc/en-us/articles/6311803642903-Use-ClickUp-as-a-guest-or-limited-member

How I got there:

Worked directly with affected participants and collected screenshots of what they were actually seeing Cross-referenced that against ClickUp's guest and limited member documentation

Where we're at:

There is a fix, and we've already applied it to 80 people according to Clickup. The remaining ~200 or so of our existing participants still need it applied.

The settings are buried and not very intuitive to find, so I'm posting screenshot steps next. It's a manual pass through a lot of users, so the more hands on it the faster everyone gets unblocked.

— David "AssassinCS" Thompson in #🗓️│production-lead-discussion (jump)
